newsitem.title: USA: Unocal to carve out 76 Products unit, mulls sale.
newsitem.headline: Unocal to carve out 76 Products unit, mulls sale.

text.p: Unocal Corp. Tuesday announced plans to separate its 76 Products Co. subsidiary from its core exploration and production businesses, moving the company a step closer to leaving California's cutthroat refining and marketing business.

Industry analysts said the move, the latest in a series of downstream divestments by Unocal, reflected intense competition in the West Coast market and a desire by Unocal to focus its resources in more lucrative overseas markets.
"Unocal no longer has any production in California... There are no synergies between refining and marketing and oil and gas production," said Bruce Lanni, an analyst with Oppenheimer & Co.

Los Angeles-based Unocal said 76 Products was formed in 1994 and controls refining, marketing, and transportation assets, but does not legally hold them. The ownership of those assets will be transferred to 76 Products Co. on Jan. 1.
Unocal said it expected to carve out the separate unit once 76 Products became consistently profitable and will consider an initial public offering, a joint venture, or an outright sale.
"The timing for implementing one of these options depends upon 76 Products' continued progress in developing sustainable earnings and cash flow," said Roger Beach, the company's chairman.

The 76 Products Co. will employ 3,100 people and hold about $2.7 billion in assets, including three refineries in California, with a combined crude oil input capacity of 251,000 barrels per day. The unit will lease or own a chain of 1,200 service stations in six western states.
Unocal's move follows the April sale of its California crude oil and natural gas assets to Nuevo Energy Co. for $492 million.
The announcement came as no surprise to Wall Street, which has watched the competition for California's refining and marketing business intensify.

Analysts in mid-October reported a sharp 21 percent decline in West Coast refining profit margins in the early weeks of the fourth quarter, reflecting rising crude oil prices and falling prices for gasoline.
"Industry-wide it hasn't been the rosiest business to be in," said Philip Tendler, an analyst for Schroder Wertheim & Co.
By comparison, the percentage of Unocal's overseas crude oil production is expected to grow in the next year to around 60 percent of its total output from about 48 percent this year.
Unocal said 76 Products will control interests in bulk plants and terminals, West Coast pipelines and a marine fleet of one crude oil tanker and two refined product tankers.
For the first nine months of 1996, the business unit reported pretax income of $128 million on revenues of $3.6 billion, Unocal said.
Unocal shares rose $1.25 to $36.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
